# Phase One — Route-Wide Mobile Surface Quality Brainstorm

## Hidden work reopened
The creation-specific gate passed, but the original user requirement is broader: the internal Social Hub should be mobile-first, every visible element should be intentionally styled, and labels/text should not drift loose. The live `RouteModel` exposes twelve social chambers, so a skeptical completion test must traverse all twelve rather than infer route-wide quality from Home and Interact alone.

## Live route universe
- home — Social pulse
- inbox — Communications Inbox
- messages — Private Messages
- spaces — Communities and channels
- people — Discover people
- profile — Public profile
- chat — Live Torah Chat
- interact — Interaction studio
- activity — Activity ledger
- network — Public network
- references — Reference graph
- privacy — Privacy controls

## Every useful audit idea
1. Open every route at the real mobile fixture width.
2. Prove the route panel becomes visible after navigation.
3. Measure document horizontal overflow after every route settles.
4. Walk visible text nodes and detect text whose parent has no visible styling/semantic vessel.
5. Detect text elements with transparent/invisible color or zero font size.
6. Detect visible elements whose rectangles escape the viewport horizontally.
7. Detect buttons/links/selects/inputs/textarea that collapse to unusable geometry.
8. Treat checkboxes/radios and explicitly hidden controls separately from ordinary touch targets.
9. Record route name with every defect so fixes are localized.
10. Avoid judging aesthetic taste through brittle color equality.
11. Prefer computed-style/geometry facts over class-name guesses.
12. Preserve intentionally text-like links that are styled through ancestor rules.
13. Do not require every word to have its own class if its semantic/styled parent is the vessel.
14. Flag direct non-whitespace text nodes under unstyled generic containers as truly loose text.
15. Audit headings, paragraphs, labels, badges, empty states, cards, controls, and navigation-triggered panels.
16. Keep persistent Create and mobile dock in the global geometry audit while route panel quality is measured separately.
17. Do not click destructive/posting controls.
18. Do not mutate server data.
19. Use the existing deterministic browser fixture.
20. Capture defect evidence before touching production.
21. If a route fails, trace its actual template/style owner before rewriting anything.
22. Add the route-wide quality audit to browser smoke so future changes cannot reintroduce naked/overflowing surfaces.
23. Keep new test helper files below 120 lines by splitting DOM inspection from route orchestration.
24. Maintain the existing one-cache-generation and local-style contracts.
25. Keep external network linking completely absent.

## Failure map
A route can look acceptable at desktop width yet overflow at 390px. A text node can inherit typography yet still float inside an unbounded generic container. A button can be visible but too small to touch. A hidden panel can pollute an audit if visibility is not checked. Dynamic route content can settle after hash navigation, so the audit must wait for active panel visibility before sampling.

## First principle
The Awtsmoos gives every revealed word a vessel and every vessel a boundary; Awtsmoos.com should let no social chamber spill beyond the hand-sized world that contains it. The browser, not confidence, will decide which chambers still need garments.
